`AGENTS.md`:

```md
# Working on this project

Notes for contributors and coding agents: how the project is laid out, how to build and test it, and
the rules that keep a test run from disturbing the machine it runs on.

## Layout

- `src/` — the hand-written part: start-up and paths (`main.c`, `install.c`, `port.h`), the settings
  (`launcher.c`, `pc_menu.c`, `ingame_menu.c`, `pause_tab.c`), input (`keyboard.c`, `bindings.c`,
  `menu_mouse.c`), game fixes and options (`cheats.c`, `movie_skip.c`, `costume_menu.c`, ...), the
  Direct3D renderer on Vulkan (`src/d3d`, see `docs/renderer.md`).
- `src/recomp/gen/` — the lifted game code, generated by `tools/pipeline.sh` from the player's disc.
  **Never commit it**, nor the game's data (`game_files/`, `disc/`, `*.xbe`, `*.afs`, saves, captures
  of the game's pictures). Only the functions taken out of it to be modified (`tools/take_function.py`,
  listed in `src/manual_functions.json`) are kept in the hand-written sources.
- `src/manual_functions.json` — lifted functions replaced by hand-written ones (the generator skips
  them); `src/icall_targets.json` — indirect-call targets the analysis missed (`tools/feedback.sh`).
- `packaging/` — the AppImage (`appimage/build.sh`, in Docker) and the Windows zip
  (`windows/build.sh`, cross-compiled with llvm-mingw); shader seeds shipped with both.
- `docs/` — `TECHNICAL.md` (how everything works), `renderer.md`.
- `xboxrecomp/` — the recompiler and Xbox runtime: [xboxrecomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp)
  with this port's changes, kept here (see `xboxrecomp/UPSTREAM.md`); its third-party sources come
  from `xboxrecomp/third_party/fetch.sh`. `-DXBOXRECOMP_DIR=` builds against another copy.

## Building

```sh
xboxrecomp/third_party/fetch.sh         # once
tools/pipeline.sh /path/to/ngb.iso      # once, and after changing the analysis inputs
cmake -S . -B build/linux -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++
ninja -C build/linux                    # build/linux/NinjaGaidenBlack
packaging/appimage/build.sh             # build/appimage/NinjaGaidenBlack-x86_64.AppImage
packaging/windows/build.sh              # build/windows-release/NinjaGaidenBlack-windows-x64.zip
```

The generated code is large: cap the memory of big builds (`systemd-run --user --scope -p
MemoryMax=14G ...`).

## Testing

Test runs must never touch the user's own data or desktop:

- **Never the real saves or settings** (`~/.local/share/NinjaGaidenBlack`, `~/.config/NinjaGaidenBlack`).
  Copy what you need into a scratch folder and point the game there: `NGB_SAVE_DIR`,
  `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `NGB_GAME_DIR`; `NGB_NO_SETTINGS=1` skips the settings screen.
- **No sound**: `SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy` and `NGB_AUDIO=0` (under Proton only the latter reaches the game).
- **No windows on the desktop**: run inside a headless gamescope, with `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY`:
  `gamescope --backend headless -W 1280 -H 720 -- ./run.sh`.
- **Kill only your own processes**, by PID (check `/proc/<pid>/environ` for your scratch paths) —
  never `pkill` a pattern.

Driving and watching a headless run:

- `RECOMP_PAD_LIVE=<file>`: append pad commands to the file (`a`, `b`, `x`, `y`, `start`, `back`,
  `white`, `black`, `lt`, `rt`, `up`/`down`/`left`/`right`, `lup:<ms>` and the other stick
  directions, `name:<ms>` to hold). It acts at the USB level, so code that reads the host's input
  (the recomp's own menu pages) does not see it — use `xdotool` on the gamescope's own X display
  (find it in the game's environment; never `:0`) for keys and the mouse.
- `NV2A_CAPTURE=<prefix>` and `NV2A_CAPTURE_EVERY=<n>`: a PPM of the presented picture every n
  frames. Keep `render_scale` low in test settings, or the captures fill `/tmp`.
- `NV2A_FPS_LOG=1`: frame rate, and `[LAT]` presentation timing.
- F7, or `NGB_TRACE_FILE=<file>` (recording starts when the file appears): every draw of the next
  frames and a small picture of each, in `~/ngb-trace-<n>` (`HOME` decides where).
- `NGB_RENDERER=xemu`: xemu's hardware-accurate renderer instead of ours — the reference for "is this
  our bug or the game's".
- `NGB_MODE_LOG=2` (2D-screen decisions per frame), `NGB_HUD_GROUP_TRACE=1` (HUD placement),
  `NGB_MOUSE_LOG=1`, `NGB_MOVIE_LOG=1`.
- `kill -USR1 <pid>`: the guest thread's backtrace and registers (not gdb: it swallows the
  single-steps the APU traps use). `RECOMP_COVER_SNAP=<prefix>` plus `kill -USR2`: which lifted
  functions ran between two signals.
- Windows builds under Proton: `umu-run` with a scratch `WINEPREFIX` and `PROTONPATH` set to the
  full path of a Proton install; settings then live in the prefix's `AppData/Roaming`.

## Conventions

- Match the surrounding code: comments say why, in plain sentences; names and idioms as nearby.
- A behaviour change gets checked in a headless run — measured (positions, timings, logs), not
  assumed — at the aspect ratios it touches (4:3, 16:9, 16:10, 21:9).
- Commits are small and describe the change; no build output, captures or game data in them.
- Shell scripts that loop over word lists should run under bash (`zsh` does not split `$var`), and
  a `pgrep -f` pattern matches its own command line.

```

`CMakeLists.txt`:

```txt
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)

# ============================================================================
# Ninja Gaiden Black - static recompilation (xboxrecomp)
#
# Native Linux (x86-64), Windows and macOS (arm64) builds. The generated code comes from the
# xboxrecomp pipeline (see README.md); it is not checked in.
# ============================================================================

project(ninja_gaiden_black C CXX)
if(APPLE AND NOT CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "^(arm64|aarch64)$")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "The macOS port currently supports Apple Silicon only")
endif()
if(WIN32)
    enable_language(RC)   # the program's icon (packaging/windows/ngb.rc)
endif()   # CXX: the GPU renderer links VMA

set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 11)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
    set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release CACHE STRING "" FORCE)
endif()

add_compile_definitions(WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN NOMINMAX)

# Bring-up build: record every indirect-branch target the title reaches, so
# tools/feedback.sh can reseed function detection with them. Applies to the
# toolkit too (its icall_feedback.c compiles to nothing without it).
option(NGB_ICALL_FEEDBACK "Record indirect-branch targets (bring-up builds)" OFF)
if(NGB_ICALL_FEEDBACK)
    add_compile_definitions(RECOMP_ICALL_FEEDBACK)
endif()

# The GPU: xemu's NV2A model with its Vulkan renderer (xboxrecomp nv2a_vk).
option(NGB_NV2A_VK "Render with the NV2A Vulkan model" ON)
set(XBOXRECOMP_NV2A_VK ${NGB_NV2A_VK} CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(XBOXRECOMP_SDL_BACKENDS ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)   # Windows: same SDL audio/input as Linux
set(XBOXRECOMP_WIN_VCPU ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)        # Windows: one virtual CPU, as on Linux

set(XBOXRECOMP_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/xboxrecomp" CACHE PATH
    "Path to the xboxrecomp toolkit root directory")
add_subdirectory(${XBOXRECOMP_DIR} ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/xboxrecomp)

# ── Recompiled code ─────────────────────────────────────────────

# CONFIGURE_DEPENDS: a regenerated tree can add or drop chunks.
file(GLOB RECOMP_GEN_SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS "src/recomp/gen/*.c")
if(NOT RECOMP_GEN_SOURCES)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "src/recomp/gen is empty: run the recomp pipeline first (README.md)")
endif()

# The generated chunks are ~2 MB of C each. They are an object library so
# their flags can differ from the hand-written code, and so a host change
# never recompiles them.
# Fonts (SIL Open Font License, assets/fonts) built into the program: the
# pause menu's pages until the game's own letters are loaded, its key labels
# (src/pause_tab.c) and the frame rate overlay (src/fps_text.c).
set(NGB_FONTS
    "EBGaramond-ExtraBoldItalic.ttf\;ngb_font_tab"
    "LiberationSerif-Regular.ttf\;ngb_font_body"
    "LiberationSerif-Bold.ttf\;ngb_font_label")
set(NGB_FONT_SOURCES)
foreach(entry ${NGB_FONTS})
    list(GET entry 0 file)
    list(GET entry 1 name)
    set(out ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/fonts/${name}.c)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${out}
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -DIN=${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/fonts/${file}
                -DOUT=${out} -DNAME=${name} -P ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/embed.cmake
        DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/fonts/${file}
                ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/embed.cmake
        VERBATIM)
    list(APPEND NGB_FONT_SOURCES ${out})
endforeach()

# The keyboard and mouse prompts (Xelu's free prompts, CC0: assets/prompts/License-Xelu.txt), the dark
# set and its blank key: each embedded, and a table of them by file name (src/pause_tab.c).
file(GLOB NGB_KEY_PNGS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/prompts/keys/*.png)
set(key_decls "")
set(key_rows "")
list(LENGTH NGB_KEY_PNGS key_count)
foreach(png ${NGB_KEY_PNGS})
    get_filename_component(stem ${png} NAME_WE)
    string(MAKE_C_IDENTIFIER "ngb_key_${stem}" sym)
    set(out ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/keys/${sym}.c)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${out}
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -DIN=${png} -DOUT=${out} -DNAME=${sym}
                -P ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/embed.cmake
        DEPENDS ${png} ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/embed.cmake
        VERBATIM)
    list(APPEND NGB_FONT_SOURCES ${out})
    string(APPEND key_decls "extern const unsigned char ${sym}[]; extern const unsigned int ${sym}_len;\n")
    string(APPEND key_rows "    { \"${stem}\", ${sym}, &${sym}_len },\n")
endforeach()
file(WRITE ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/keys/key_table.c.in
     "/* Generated by CMakeLists.txt: the embedded key prompts by name. */\n${key_decls}"
     "const struct { const char *name; const unsigned char *data; const unsigned int *len; } ngb_key_pngs[] = {\n"
     "${key_rows}};\nconst int ngb_key_png_count = ${key_count};\n")
configure_file(${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/keys/key_table.c.in ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/keys/key_table.c COPYONLY)
list(APPEND NGB_FONT_SOURCES ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/keys/key_table.c)

add_library(ngb_gen OBJECT ${RECOMP_GEN_SOURCES}
    # Hand-written replacements in the generated code's style.
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/movie_skip.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/costume_menu.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pc_menu.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/pause_tab.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/menu_mouse.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/menu_font.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/fps_text.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/playtime.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/main_menu.c
    # The Direct3D hooks (docs/renderer.md, tools/take_d3d.py).
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/d3d/d3d.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/cheats.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/d3d/d3d_hooks.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/d3d/d3d_orig.c
    ${NGB_FONT_SOURCES})
target_include_directories(ngb_gen PRIVATE
    ${XBOXRECOMP_DIR}/third_party/stb
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/recomp/gen
    ${XBOXRECOMP_DIR}/include
    ${XBOXRECOMP_DIR}/src
    ${XBOXRECOMP_DIR}/src/kernel
)
target_link_libraries(ngb_gen PRIVATE platform)
if(NGB_NV2A_VK)
    find_package(SDL2 REQUIRED)   # SDL's key codes (src/pause_tab.c's key prompts)
    target_include_directories(ngb_gen PRIVATE $<TARGET_PROPERTY:SDL2::SDL2,INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES>)
endif()

if(MSVC)
    target_compile_options(ngb_gen PRIVATE /bigobj /O2)
else()
    # The guest memory model aliases freely through MEM32/MEMF; strict
    # aliasing would let the optimiser reorder guest loads and stores.
    # Lifted code is one big function per guest routine, so the flags that
    # make a function's codegen superlinear are capped.
    target_compile_options(ngb_gen PRIVATE
        -O2 -fno-strict-aliasing -fwrapv
        -Wno-unused-label -Wno-unused-variable -Wno-unused-but-set-variable
        -Wno-parentheses-equality -Wno-tautological-compare
        -Wno-incompatible-pointer-types-discards-qualifiers
    )
endif()

# ── The Direct3D renderer (docs/renderer.md, src/d3d/NOTICE) ────

if(NGB_NV2A_VK)
    if(APPLE)
        find_package(glslang CONFIG REQUIRED)
    endif()
    set(XRTP ${XBOXRECOMP_DIR}/third_party)
    add_library(ngb_d3d OBJECT
        src/d3d/hle.cpp
        src/d3d/vk/backend.cpp
        src/d3d/vk/spirv.cpp
        src/d3d/gpu/shaders.cpp
        src/d3d/gpu/vertex.cpp
        src/d3d/gpu/texture.cpp)
    target_include_directories(ngb_d3d PRIVATE
        src
        src/d3d src/d3d/compat ${XBOXRECOMP_DIR}/src/nv2a_vk/host
        ${XRTP}/Vulkan-Headers/include ${XRTP}/volk ${XRTP}/VulkanMemoryAllocator/include)
    target_compile_definitions(ngb_d3d PRIVATE VK_NO_PROTOTYPES
        VMA_STATIC_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS=0 VMA_DYNAMIC_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS=0)
    if(APPLE)
        target_link_libraries(ngb_d3d PRIVATE glslang::glslang glslang::glslang-default-resource-limits)
    endif()
    target_compile_features(ngb_d3d PRIVATE cxx_std_20)
    target_compile_options(ngb_d3d PRIVATE -O2 -fno-strict-aliasing)
endif()

# ── Executable ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

add_executable(${PROJECT_NAME}
    src/main.c
    src/recomp_manual.c
    src/fibers.c
    $<$<BOOL:${NGB_NV2A_VK}>:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/launcher.c>
    $<$<BOOL:${NGB_NV2A_VK}>:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/ingame_menu.c>
    $<$<BOOL:${NGB_NV2A_VK}>:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/keyboard.c>
    $<$<BOOL:${NGB_NV2A_VK}>:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/bindings.c>
    src/install.c
    $<TARGET_OBJECTS:ngb_gen>
    $<$<BOOL:${NGB_NV2A_VK}>:$<TARGET_OBJECTS:ngb_d3d>>
    $<$<PLATFORM_ID:Windows>:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/packaging/windows/ngb.rc>
)
target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE xboxrecomp)
if(WIN32)   # the resource script includes these: rebuilt when they change, not only ngb.rc
    set_source_files_properties(${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/packaging/windows/ngb.rc PROPERTIES OBJECT_DEPENDS
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/packaging/windows/ngb.manifest;${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/packaging/windows/ngb.ico")
endif()
if(NGB_NV2A_VK)
    target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE xbox_nv2a_vk)
    target_compile_definitions(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE NGB_NV2A_VK)
endif()
target_include_directories(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/recomp/gen
    ${XBOXRECOMP_DIR}/include
    ${XBOXRECOMP_DIR}/src
)

if(WIN32)
    # A GUI program (no console window); main() attaches to a parent console.
    set_target_properties(${PROJECT_NAME} PROPERTIES OUTPUT_NAME NinjaGaidenBlack
                          WIN32_EXECUTABLE TRUE)
    target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE
        winmm dbghelp comdlg32 comctl32 shell32 ole32)
    if(MSVC)
        target_link_options(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE /LARGEADDRESSAWARE)
    endif()
else()
    set_target_properties(${PROJECT_NAME} PROPERTIES OUTPUT_NAME NinjaGaidenBlack)
    # -rdynamic: the crash handler names the faulting sub_XXXXXXXX via dladdr.
    target_link_options(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE -rdynamic)
    target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE ${CMAKE_DL_LIBS} m)
endif()

# ── First-run setup window (Qt) ─────────────────────────────────
# ngb-setup asks for the player's disc and installs it (src/install.c); the
# game runs it from beside itself when it finds no game files. Optional:
# without Qt the game asks through zenity/kdialog.
if(NOT WIN32)
    find_package(Qt6 QUIET COMPONENTS Widgets)
    if(Qt6_FOUND)
        set(CMAKE_AUTORCC ON)
        add_executable(ngb-setup src/setup/ngb_setup.cpp src/setup/setup.qrc src/install.c)
        target_link_libraries(ngb-setup PRIVATE Qt6::Widgets)
        set_target_properties(ngb-setup PROPERTIES CXX_STANDARD 17
            RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})
        message(STATUS "ngb-setup: Qt ${Qt6_VERSION}")
    else()
        message(STATUS "ngb-setup: no Qt6 Widgets, not built")
    endif()
endif()

`README.md`:

```md
![Ninja Gaiden Black Recompiled](docs/images/banner.jpg)

# Ninja Gaiden Black Recompiled

**A PC port of Ninja Gaiden Black by static recompilation.**

A native Linux and Windows version of *Ninja Gaiden Black* (Xbox, 2005), made by statically
recompiling the game's own code to run directly on a PC — not an emulator. It draws with its own
Vulkan renderer, which takes over the game's Direct3D calls instead of emulating the Xbox GPU. It
plays at a steady 60 fps on modest hardware (including the Steam Deck) and adds PC options: higher
resolutions, widescreen and ultrawide, keyboard and mouse, rebindable controls and more.

**You need your own copy of the game.** This project contains none of the game's data (graphics,
sound, movies, text): on first start it asks for your disc image and installs the game from it. It is made for the **retail USA
release** (NTSC-U, title ID `5443000D`) and checks for it.

## Features

- Native Linux (AppImage) and Windows (x64) builds; Steam Deck friendly
- Render resolution up to 10x, anisotropic filtering, MSAA, sharper shadows
- 16:9, 16:10 and 21:9 as well as 4:3: the 3D fills the screen, the HUD goes to the screen's
  corners, menus keep the game's own 16:9 look
- Keyboard and mouse with key prompts in the game, rebindable controls for keyboard, mouse and
  controller, mouse support in the menus
- Skippable intros and movies, unlock-all options for difficulties and costumes, optional cheats
- Smooth frame pacing and low input latency; shaders prepared in the background (no first-time
  stutter)

## Getting started

### Linux and Steam Deck

1. Download `NinjaGaidenBlack-x86_64.AppImage` from the releases page and make it executable
   (`chmod +x`, or Properties → Allow executing).
2. Run it. On the first start a window asks for your copy of the game: a disc image (`.iso`, a full
   Redump dump, or the `.7z`/`.zip` it came in) or a folder of extracted files with `default.xbe`.
   The game is installed once (about 6 GB).
3. On a Steam Deck, add the AppImage to Steam (Add a Non-Steam Game) to play it in Game Mode, and
   choose 16:10 in the settings.

Needs a 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer and a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 drivers.

### Windows

1. Download `NinjaGaidenBlack-windows-x64.zip` and extract it anywhere.
2. Run `NinjaGaidenBlack.exe` and choose your disc image as above.

Needs Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 drivers.

### macOS (experimental)

Build the Apple Silicon app using the commands below, extract the resulting zip, and open
`Ninja Gaiden Black.app`. Choose your own disc image or extracted game folder on first start.
Current dependencies require macOS 26. Intel Macs and the xemu renderer are unsupported;
packages are signed ad hoc, without Developer ID signing or notarization.

### Where things are kept

| | Linux | Windows | macOS |
|---|---|---|---|
| Installed game, saves | `~/.local/share/NinjaGaidenBlack` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NinjaGaidenBlack` | `~/Library/Application Support/NinjaGaidenBlack/saves` |
| Settings (`settings.ini`, `controls.ini`) | `~/.config/NinjaGaidenBlack` | `%APPDATA%\NinjaGaidenBlack` | `~/Library/Application Support/NinjaGaidenBlack/config` |
| Shader cache | `~/.cache/NinjaGaidenBlack` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NinjaGaidenBlack\shaders` | `~/Library/Application Support/NinjaGaidenBlack/cache/NinjaGaidenBlack/shaders` |
| Log | the terminal | `log.txt` beside the saves (or the console it was started from) | `log.txt` beside the saves |

**Portable mode:** with a file named `portable.txt` next to `NinjaGaidenBlack.exe` (or the AppImage or Mac app),
all of these go into a `userdata` folder next to it instead. The first-run setup offers this as a
checkbox. The folder must be writable, so not inside Program Files. Delete `portable.txt` to go back.

## Settings

Everything is in the game's own menus: **RECOMP SETTINGS** on the main menu, and the **Settings** tab
of the pause menu. Changes apply at once and are saved.

- **Graphics**: render resolution (1x–10x), texture filtering (the console's, or 2x–16x
  anisotropic), anti-aliasing (MSAA), shadow resolution
- **Display**: aspect ratio (4:3, 16:9, 16:10, 21:9), window size, windowed / fullscreen /
  borderless, V-Sync (Off, Mailbox, FIFO, Adaptive), frame-rate counter
- **Startup**: skip the warnings and intro movies, all difficulties from the start, all costumes
- **Cheats** (for the session only): infinite health, ninpo, essence; golden scarabs
- **Controls**: rebind every action (two keys or mouse buttons and a controller button each)

The game's own Options (sound, movie aspect, controller vibration and so on) are where they always
were.

## Controls

A controller works as on the Xbox. The keyboard and mouse can be used at any time — the game follows
whichever was touched last, and its button prompts change to match.

| Action | Keys | | Action | Keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Move | W A S D | | Camera | mouse (numpad 8 4 5 6) |
| Attack | left mouse, J | | Special attack | right mouse, K |
| Jump | Space | | Projectile | E |
| Ninpo | F | | Wind run | C |
| Guard / roll | Shift | | Center camera | Q, middle mouse |
| Map | Tab | | Karma window | R |
| Pause | Esc, Enter | | First-person view | Z |

After loading, the right stick (or the mouse) looks around in first person, as on the Xbox; click the
right stick (V) to turn the third-person camera instead. **Invert Camera X / Y** (RECOMP SETTINGS →
Controls) flips the stick and mouse for both; the game's own Options → Controller Settings → 1st Person
Camera Control can flip first-person look back.

In the menus the mouse points and clicks, Esc goes back and Q / E switch the pause menu's tabs.
Movies can be skipped with Start, A or B (or the keys for them); in-game cutscenes with Start.

Other keys: **F10** frame-rate counter, **F11** or **Alt+Enter** fullscreen.

## Known issues

- **Water** in some places (the pond in Chapter 2, for example) can look banded instead of clear, so
  far reported on Nvidia cards on Windows (#16).
- **Controller vibration on Windows** may only start working after switching Vibration off and on
  again in the game's Options (#15).
- **Installing directly from an ISO** fails on some Windows PCs (#6, #14). Until that is fixed:
  extract the ISO to a folder named `game` next to `NinjaGaidenBlack.exe`, and it is found
  automatically.
- **Steam Deck:** do the first start (installing the game) in Desktop Mode. In Game Mode the window
  to choose your disc image cannot open, and the game closes (#11).
- The **Ninja Gaiden arcade cabinet** in Han's bar does not work: the game closes when you play it
  (#18). The NES games are a separate program on the disc (`NinjaTrilogy.xbe`) that the Xbox switches
  to, and only Ninja Gaiden Black itself is recompiled. Save before trying it.
- At **21:9**, objects at the far left and right of the screen can appear a moment late (the game
  decides what to draw for a narrower view).
- The Windows build has been tested under Proton and in a Windows 11 virtual machine; reports from
  real Windows PCs are especially welcome.

When reporting a graphics glitch, pressing **F7** while it is on screen records the next few seconds of
drawing to `~/ngb-trace-<n>` on Linux, or `C:\Users\<you>\ngb-trace-<n>` on Windows — attach that
folder (zipped), it shows exactly what went wrong.

## Building from source

The build needs the game's code, so it starts from your own disc image.

Requirements: clang, CMake, Ninja, Python 3, git, SDL2, GLib, glslang and SPIRV-Tools (Qt 6
Widgets for the setup window, optional). The recompiler and Xbox runtime,
[xboxrecomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp) with this port's changes, is included in
`xboxrecomp/`.

```sh
xboxrecomp/third_party/fetch.sh                # once: Vulkan headers, volk, VMA and the like
tools/pipeline.sh /path/to/your/ngb.iso        # extract, disassemble and lift to C (a few minutes)
cmake -S . -B build/linux -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++
ninja -C build/linux
build/linux/NinjaGaidenBlack
```

Packages: `packaging/appimage/build.sh` (in a Docker container, for an AppImage that runs on older
systems), `packaging/windows/build.sh` (cross-compiled from Linux with llvm-mingw), and
`packaging/macos/build.sh` (native Apple Silicon). Packages contain no game data.

On macOS, install the build dependencies below, then run the fetch and pipeline steps above
and package the app:

```sh
brew install cmake ninja sdl2-compat sdl3 libepoxy glib glslang molten-vk vulkan-loader qt
packaging/macos/build.sh
```

The zip is `build/macos-release/NinjaGaidenBlack-macos-arm64.zip`. Homebrew is needed only to
build; runtime libraries, including MoltenVK, are bundled. `NGB_MAC_PREFIX` overrides the build
dependency prefix (default: `brew --prefix`).

How it works, and the details of every feature: [docs/TECHNICAL.md](docs/TECHNICAL.md) and
[docs/renderer.md](docs/renderer.md). For contributors and coding agents: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## The game

*Ninja Gaiden Black* © Koei Tecmo / Team Ninja. None of the game's data (graphics, sound, movies,
text) is in this repository, and its recompiled code is generated from the player's own copy when
building (`tools/pipeline.sh`); the game's data is installed from it on the first start. The
repository does include C translations of some of the game's functions, taken from that generated code
and modified for this port (the menus, the mouse, the cheats: `src/main_menu.c`, `src/pause_tab.c`,
`src/menu_mouse.c` and others, listed in `src/manual_functions.json`), and the Direct3D functions of
the Xbox SDK the game was built with (`src/d3d/d3d_orig.c`), behind the renderer's hooks.

`cmake/embed.cmake`:

```cmake
# cmake -DIN=<file> -DOUT=<file.c> -DNAME=<symbol> -P embed.cmake
# A file's bytes as `const unsigned char NAME[]` and `NAME_len`.
file(READ "${IN}" hex HEX)
string(LENGTH "${hex}" n)
math(EXPR len "${n} / 2")
string(REGEX REPLACE "([0-9a-f][0-9a-f])" "0x\\1," bytes "${hex}")
string(REGEX REPLACE "(0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,0x..,)" "\\1\n" bytes "${bytes}")
file(WRITE "${OUT}" "/* Generated from ${IN} by cmake/embed.cmake. */\n"
     "const unsigned char ${NAME}[] = {\n${bytes}\n};\n"
     "const unsigned int ${NAME}_len = ${len};\n")

```

`cmake/toolchains/windows-x64-llvm-mingw.cmake`:

```cmake
# Cross-compile for Windows x64 from Linux with llvm-mingw (clang, lld, libc++, UCRT) against
# MSYS2's CLANG64 packages (SDL2, glib, glslang, SPIRV-Tools) unpacked into a sysroot.
# packaging/windows/build.sh fetches both into build/windows-deps.
set(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME Windows)
set(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR AMD64)
set(NGB_WIN_DEPS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/../../build/windows-deps" CACHE PATH "llvm-mingw and the CLANG64 sysroot")
file(GLOB _llvm_mingw "${NGB_WIN_DEPS}/llvm-mingw-*-ucrt-*")
list(GET _llvm_mingw 0 _llvm_mingw)
set(_triple x86_64-w64-mingw32)
set(CMAKE_C_COMPILER "${_llvm_mingw}/bin/${_triple}-clang")
set(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER "${_llvm_mingw}/bin/${_triple}-clang++")
set(CMAKE_RC_COMPILER "${_llvm_mingw}/bin/${_triple}-windres")
set(CMAKE_AR "${_llvm_mingw}/bin/llvm-ar")
set(CMAKE_RANLIB "${_llvm_mingw}/bin/llvm-ranlib")
set(NGB_WIN_SYSROOT "${NGB_WIN_DEPS}/sysroot/clang64")
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH "${NGB_WIN_SYSROOT}" "${_llvm_mingw}/${_triple}")
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_PROGRAM NEVER)
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_LIBRARY ONLY)
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_INCLUDE ONLY)
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_PACKAGE ONLY)
set(CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH "${NGB_WIN_SYSROOT}")
# pkg-config: the sysroot's .pc files only
set(ENV{PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR} "${NGB_WIN_SYSROOT}/lib/pkgconfig:${NGB_WIN_SYSROOT}/share/pkgconfig")
set(ENV{PKG_CONFIG_SYSROOT_DIR} "${NGB_WIN_DEPS}/sysroot")
set(ENV{PKG_CONFIG_PATH} "")
# The sysroot's headers for every target (glslang's for the renderer, which links it through xboxrecomp)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES "${NGB_WIN_SYSROOT}/include")
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES "${NGB_WIN_SYSROOT}/include")

```

`docs/TECHNICAL.md`:

```md
# Ninja Gaiden Black — technical notes

How the recompilation works and how its PC features are built, for whoever works on it. The
player-facing summary is the README; how to build and test is in AGENTS.md.

## How it runs

The game's x86 code (`default.xbe`) is disassembled and lifted to C by
[xboxrecomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp)'s pipeline (`tools/pipeline.sh`: about
11.5k functions, 2.2M lines, written to `src/recomp/gen/`, never committed -- it is made from the
player's own disc) and compiled for the host. Nothing is emulated at the CPU level. The rest of the
console is xboxrecomp's runtime:

- **Kernel**: the Xbox kernel's services (threads, files, memory, the hard disk's partitions as
  sparse image files) on the host's.
- **One virtual CPU** (`platform/vcpu.h`): the Xbox has a single CPU and a priority scheduler, and
  the game depends on it (a thread made ready above the running one runs at once). Guest threads
  share one token; waits give it up; a higher-priority thread preempts the holder -- on Linux with a
  signal, on Windows by suspending it and redirecting it into a yield (`vcpu_win_trampoline`).
- **GPU**: xemu's NV2A model runs the game's command stream (fences, vertical blanks, flips); the
  drawing is done by a renderer of the game's Direct3D calls on Vulkan (below).
- **Audio**: the MCPX APU's voice processor (from xemu) mixing into SDL2's output.
- **Input**: SDL2 controllers, keyboard and mouse, as the Xbox's USB pad through an OHCI model.

`kill -USR1 <pid>` (Linux) prints the guest thread's host backtrace, every lifted function a named
`sub_XXXXXXXX`, and its guest registers -- use it instead of gdb, which swallows the TF single-steps
the APU and AC97 register traps depend on.

## Windows

The same code, cross-compiled with llvm-mingw against MSYS2 CLANG64 libraries
(`packaging/windows/build.sh`, `cmake/toolchains/windows-x64-llvm-mingw.cmake`). It uses the same
host backends as Linux (`XBOXRECOMP_SDL_BACKENDS`: SDL2 audio and input, no XInput, XAudio2 or
Media Foundation) and the virtual CPU (`XBOXRECOMP_WIN_VCPU`: `platform/win32_host.c`, and
`platform/win32_vcpu.h` force-included to route the Win32 waits through it). The guest's 4 GB
window is one placeholder reservation (`VirtualAlloc2`) whose regions are mapped in place. Notes:
clang targeting MinGW accepts `__declspec(thread)` but makes a plain global of it (thread-local
storage must be keyed on `_MSC_VER`); `<windows.h>` is in every file there (its `near` and `far`
macros); Windows sleeps in milliseconds, so sub-millisecond waits use a high-resolution waitable
timer (`vcpu_nap_us`). Under Proton, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `SDL_AUDIODRIVER` do not reach the game.

## Presentation

The game's frame clock is the emulated display's 60 Hz vblank. Each picture the renderer finishes
(at the game's Swap, a couple of milliseconds after a vblank) is presented at once from the
renderer's thread (`present_sdl.c`, `nv2a_present_set_external`); the vblank tick presents only what
was not (a loading pause). Presented at the tick, every frame waited a whole refresh; through the
GPU-command thread, presents came out unevenly. V-Sync's Mailbox is mailbox where the system has it
(no tearing, no queue: a FIFO queue fills against the game's own clock and adds 30-50 ms), FIFO on as
few images as allowed where it has not; its FIFO is FIFO (every frame in turn: steadier where
mailbox, like Nvidia's Fast sync, now and then shows a frame twice, #17); Off is immediate. `NV2A_FPS_LOG=1` logs the frame rate and
`[LAT]` lines: each picture's age when presented and the spacing of presents.

## Settings, menus and features

The settings are in the game's own menus, in its style: the main menu's RECOMP SETTINGS
(where Ranking was) opens the Options screen on them -- Graphics, Display and Startup
Settings and Cheats, each a page of rows like Video Settings', and Controls (the bindings' panel,
below), under a SETTINGS header (`src/pc_menu.c`;
the header and category words are drawn in Liberation Serif in the game's pictures' style,
`src/pause_tab.c`) -- and the pause menu has a Settings tab before Exit (A to enter its page,
left/right on the category strip at its top for Graphics, Display, Startup, Cheats or Controls,
up/down for the rows, left/right or A to change one -- or a click: on a value's left half back,
anywhere else on the row on -- B to leave; L and R go on to the next tab, as on the
game's own pages; `NGB_NO_SETTINGS_TAB=1` leaves the game's six tabs). They are: aspect ratio
(4:3, the game's own 4:3 mode; 16:9, its widescreen; 16:10, widescreen with the 3D drawn for
16:10; it applies at once: the 3D view's projection, the presenter and the window, whose sizes
follow the shape -- only the paused picture behind the pause menu keeps the old shape until
play resumes. The game has one layout for its HUD and menus, drawn for 4:3: in 16:9 and 16:10
they are stretched sideways, as the console did on a widescreen TV), window size (the sizes offered match the
aspect ratio), windowed/fullscreen/borderless (a frameless window over the whole display),
render resolution (1x-10x), anisotropic filtering (Off, the console's own filtering; 2x, 4x,
8x or 16x: trilinear blending between mipmaps and anisotropic filtering at that level, and
mipmaps made for the many textures the game gives none -- DXT ones decoded for it -- which stops
rock, wood and gold-leaf textures sparkling and crawling in the distance as the camera moves), anti-aliasing (MSAA Off, 2x, 4x
or 8x: the display-sized targets drawn multisampled and resolved as each pass ends; with the
new renderer only), shadow resolution (Ryu's shadow map at 2x, 4x, 8x or 10x the original
128x128, for smooth instead of blocky edges), V-Sync (Off, Mailbox, FIFO, or Adaptive:
synced, but a late frame is shown at once instead of waiting a refresh -- Vulkan's FIFO relaxed), an FPS
counter, and skipping the intros (the boot movie, which the game itself will not let you skip;
the New Game prologue and the story movies play, and Start, A or B ends any of them; from the
next start). They are saved to `~/.config/NinjaGaidenBlack/settings.ini` as they change.
`--settings` shows the old settings screen before the game.

All Difficulties (Startup, saved): New Game offers every difficulty, Ninja Dog to Master Ninja,
without clearing the one before (or dying for Ninja Dog). The game's menus ask one function (sub_001DB520, now in
`src/cheats.c`) for their unlock flags -- 7-9 are those three, read from the system data --
and with the setting on it answers yes for them; nothing is written, so the player's own record
is untouched and turning it off puts back what they have earned. Off, Ninja Dog is as the game
has it: offered after dying in chapter 1.

Cheats, for getting past a hard spot (`src/cheats.c`, applied each frame; for the session
only, never saved, so a new start has them off): Infinite Health (Ryu's health refilled each
frame -- the game keeps it per segment at 0x58A534, maxima at 0x58A524, and 0x58A566 is their
sum; a single blow taking all of it at once still kills), Infinite Ninpo (0x58A56C/0x58A56E),
Infinite Essence (0x589570, the game's cap of 99,999) and Golden Scarabs (enough in the bag --
inventory slots at 0x5891D0, item 0x59 -- to make 50 with those already given to Muramasa,
0x589574: every one of his rewards at the next visit). The game guards its state with 24
checksums (sub_00164E50) and returns to the title when one changes without the flag its own
code sets (0x7F1A94 + n); a cheat that writes sets them all. Startup Settings also has All
Costumes (saved): the Costume Selection at New Game offers every costume, as after clearing
the game, through the same flag function as All Difficulties (flags 1-4). The game has eight costumes (chr_ryu.afs, chr_ryua-g.afs) and its Costume Selection
lists five (0 and 4-7, the table at 0x3E9D10), the locked ones as white shapes; here it lists only
those unlocked (`src/costume_menu.c`), and with All Costumes on costumes 1-3 too, after the game's five:
the game has no pictures of them, so each is its default costume's picture as a silhouette with
the name across it (EXTRA 1-3, made at run time from the player's copy, `src/pause_tab.c`).
Debugging aids there: `NGB_CHEATS=111` turns them on at start, `NGB_POKE=addr:bytes:value,...`
writes guest memory every frame (only while the file `NGB_POKE_GATE` names exists, if set) and
`NGB_MEMDUMP=<dir>` dumps the 64 MB of guest memory each time `<dir>/dump.now` appears.

Back from OPTIONS or RECOMP SETTINGS the main menu's cursor returns to the entry chosen (the
game puts it where OPTIONS was before it moved, the last entry: now EXIT TO DESKTOP). With All
Difficulties' Ninja Dog the difficulty selection has five rows, a case the game never shows
there: they are spaced closer (38 instead of 44) so the first clears the header.

On a wide screen (16:9, 16:10, 21:9) the game is in its own widescreen mode the whole time, with
its 3D drawn for the screen's shape (both of its aspect constants, 0x414AF4 and 0x414AF8, are that
shape): every menu, the HUD, chapter cards and clear screens are the game's own 16:9 ones, drawn as it
draws them for a widescreen TV, kept 16:9 (`src/d3d/vk/backend.cpp`): at 21:9 narrowed to the middle
16:9, at 16:10 shortened to it, a 2D screen or menu whole there with bars beyond (at the sides at
21:9, above and below at 16:10). The bars are filled with the screen's own colours: each side's edge,
16 bands of it, sampled over the screen's first 2 s and then kept still, so a menu's animation does
not move them (`EdgeSample`; `NGB_BAR_FILL=0` makes them black). A menu drawn over the paused game
(the save statue's) has the paused game around it instead. Which frames are 2D screens: a menu
running in the frame, or (the frame before was one) no 3D drawn in this frame so far. In play the 3D fills the screen and the HUD keeps its 16:9 shape but goes
to the screen's corners and sides: each frame its pieces are grouped into elements (pieces within a few
pixels of each other -- a gauge with its caps and the words under it, the health bar with the karma, a
prompt with its icon, a line of subtitles), and each element keeps to the nearer side (or the middle,
when it is about the middle), to the top when it starts near the top (the health bar, the karma
window opened below it with it), the bottom when it ends near the bottom, else the middle; only what
is drawn after the frame's 3D counts (the 3D's own screen-space mist and spray are left as drawn), and
screen effects in play -- anything covering most of the screen or reading a render target: the
underwater tint, flashes, the bloom -- fill the whole screen as drawn (`HudGroup`, `HudPlace`;
`NGB_HUD_GROUP_LOG=1` logs them, `NGB_HUD_CENTER=1` keeps the whole HUD in the middle 16:9). A screen
of panels drawn over the game (a chapter clear: an element about the middle of the screen, over a third
of its width and nearly half its height, across its middle -- an area's name is not one -- for 4 frames
running; over after 8 without) is kept whole in
the middle, as a menu: what is inside the panel's box goes with it, the HUD around it stays where it is. At 4:3 the game is in its 4:3 mode and everything is its 4:3 picture.
(Earlier versions kept the game in its 4:3 mode in play and narrowed its HUD to its 4:3 shape,
switching modes for the menus; the screens it could not tell apart in time -- item pickups, chapter
clears, leaving the save menu -- came out half one way and half the other. `NGB_HUD_FIXED=1` brings
that back, for comparison.) Movies play in the widescreen mode too, where the game follows its own Movie Display
Ratio (Options, Video Settings): 16:9 across the screen, or 4:3 with bars at the sides. (Switching to
its 4:3 mode for a 4:3 movie narrowed it twice, #28.) The mouse is mapped to the menus the same way.
`NGB_HUD_RATIO_LOG=1` logs the 2D draws not drawn texel for pixel; `NGB_MODE_LOG=1` the mode each
frame.
Aspect ratio also offers 21:9 (64:27;
window sizes 1720x720 to 5120x2160): the 3D widened as for 16:10, the game deciding what to
draw for a narrower view, so objects at the far edges may appear late.

The boot "Warnings" screen is always skipped (`NGB_KEEP_WARNINGS=1` shows it).

For glitches that only show in play: F7 records the next 300 frames to `~/ngb-trace-<n>/` -- a
small picture of each frame and a line per draw (its state: targets, textures, combiner stages,
blending, fog, vertex colour, clears) in `draws.txt` (`NGB_TRACE_FRAMES=<n>` frames;
`NGB_TRACE_PRE=1` only the screen-space draws and the first draw after each target change;
`NGB_TRACE_NOPIC=1` no pictures, `=copy` pictures only around a copy into a 512x512 target, the
cut cross-fade's). F8 appends Ryu's position to `ngb_positions.txt`
in the save directory.

The pause menu's Exit tab has a page of its own: Return to Game (the game's Exit: the menu
closes), Return to Main Menu and Exit to Desktop, the last two after an "Are you sure?"
Yes/No box in the game's menus' style (a near-black panel between gold rules, the game's own
letters, the chosen answer white in the violet haze of its menu items). The main menu's last entry is EXIT TO DESKTOP, behind the same box (OPTIONS moved
up into the never-shown COMING ATTRACTIONS' place). The game has no way back to its title
from play but the console's reset, so Return to Main Menu starts the program again in the
same process (Steam and the like see one game running throughout), skips the intros and
presses Start at the title; the window closes and opens again on the way.

F11 or Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen and
F10 the FPS counter (frames per second, average and worst frame time over the last half
second). Compiled shaders are kept in `~/.cache/NinjaGaidenBlack/shaders` (the new renderer's in its
`d3d` folder: how each shader is made, its SPIR-V and the pipelines), and all of them are made
again in the background at the next start, before the game needs them; a seed shipped with the
AppImage (`packaging/d3d-seed.bin`, recorded over the first chapters; the game's vertex programs in
it are only places in the player's own `default.xbe`) does the same on the very first start. So
an effect does not stutter the frame it first appears. The AppImage also carries the pipelines
recorded while testing (`packaging/shader-seed`), built in the background at startup;
the game's vertex programs are not in it, only where each is in `default.xbe`, and they are
read from the player's own copy (`tools/strip_shader_seed.py` makes the seed from a
recorded shader cache).

(The main menu's Video Settings page has no PC row: the settings are under RECOMP SETTINGS.)

Keyboard and mouse: whichever of them or a controller was used last is the one the game listens
to (touch the other and it switches; xboxrecomp's input). The keys by default (`src/keyboard.c`;
the game's default actions in brackets):

| Keys | Pad | | Keys | Pad |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W A S D | left stick (move) | | mouse, numpad 8 4 5 6 | right stick |
| left mouse, J | X (attack) | | right mouse, K | Y (special attack) |
| Space | A (jump) | | E | B (projectile) |
| F | Y+B (ninpo) | | C | X+A (wind run) |
| Shift | L (guard) | | Q, middle mouse | R (center camera) |
| Tab | Black (map) | | R | White (karma window) |
| Esc, Enter | START | | Backspace | BACK |
| arrows | d-pad | | Z / V | stick clicks |

Controls (the Settings tab's Controls category and RECOMP SETTINGS' CONTROLS; the game's own
Options > Controller Settings > Button Settings is left as the game has it, for the controller)
changes them: each action in play has two keys or mouse
buttons and a controller button; A (Enter, a click) waits for the new one -- Esc cancels; for the
controller, its next button, or six seconds -- and X (Delete) clears it. A key taken from another
action leaves it; a controller button taken from another action swaps with it. They are kept in
`controls.ini` beside `settings.ini` (`src/bindings.c`); in play the keyboard and mouse press the
pad as bound and the controller's buttons are moved to their actions (`xbox_pad_remap`, weak in
xboxrecomp's input). The sticks are not moved; the menus keep their own controls, the controller
as it is, so no binding can lock them up. Play's key prompts follow the bindings.
`NGB_FIXED_KEYS=1` keeps the keys above, `NGB_NO_PAD_REMAP=1` the controller as it is,
`NGB_CONTROLS_IN_OPTIONS=1` puts the panel over the game's Button Settings too.

In the menus Esc is B (back), Q and E are L and R (the pause menu's tabs) and the mouse points;
in play the mouse is captured and its motion is the right stick. The pointer is shown only in the
menus while the keyboard and mouse are in use. While the keyboard is in use the
game's button prompts are keys and mouse buttons instead -- Xelu's dark keyboard and mouse prompts
(CC0, `assets/prompts/keys`, the same artist's as the controller buttons; a key the set has no picture
of, its blank key with the key's name; `src/pause_tab.c`), in play the ones bound to each action, in
the menus the mouse's buttons (left to choose, right to go back), K, Space, Shift and Q/E;
`NGB_PAD_PROMPTS=1` keeps the pad's.

In the game's menus (main menu, Options, the pause menu and its tabs, message boxes) the mouse
points: the game's own cursor follows it onto the item under it (a press of the pad at a time,
so the game moves it as it would), a click there chooses it, a right click is B, the wheel
up/down, the side buttons the triggers. While a controller is the device in use it does
nothing in the menus; moving it makes the keyboard and mouse the device in use again. (`NGB_MOUSE_LOG=1` shows what it finds.)

The button prompts ("Select", "Back") can be clicked: the button they show. Esc is B (back) in
the game's menus.

The main menu has RECOMP SETTINGS in Ranking's place (Xbox Live's scoreboards, gone; choosing it
sent the game to the dashboard's account setup, which closed the program) and Options > General Settings no Flag
Select (the country the scoreboards wanted) -- `src/main_menu.c`; `NGB_KEEP_RANKING=1` keeps
both.

Total Play Time: saves made by builds before the clock fix hold the 999:59 cap (the PC's uptime
was counted); such a total is started again from 0 when loaded (`src/playtime.c`).

The environment still overrides the file, for testing: `NGB_WIDESCREEN=0|1`,
`NGB_FULLSCREEN=0|1`, `NGB_VSYNC=0|1`, `NV2A_SCALE=n`, `NV2A_SHOW_FPS=1`,
`NGB_NO_SETTINGS=1` (skip the screen), `NGB_AUDIO=0` (mute). `NV2A_FPS_LOG=1` prints the
FPS counter to stderr, and `NV2A_FPS_LOG=/path/to/file` appends it to that file (on a Steam Deck:
`NV2A_FPS_LOG=/home/deck/ngb-fps.txt %command%` as the launch options). `NV2A_EARLY_PRESENT=1` shows a finished frame before the title flips to it
(a refresh less latency); off by default, because on a busy frame it made the rate fall to 40-50.
`NV2A_REFRESH_HZ=n` runs the emulated display at n Hz (testing only: the game steps its logic
once a frame, so at 120 it plays at double speed).

## The renderer

The game is drawn by a renderer that implements its Direct3D calls on Vulkan (`src/d3d`,
`docs/renderer.md`; its shader translation, vertex and texture code come from TGP482's
[SCDA-XBERecomp](https://github.com/TGP482/SCDA-XBERecomp) /
[Xbox-XBERecomp](https://github.com/TGP482/Xbox-XBERecomp), MIT). xemu's NV2A
emulation still runs the GPU's command stream (the game's fences and vertical blanks come from
it) but draws nothing; the renderer draws on the same Vulkan device and the same window, so the
settings and the FPS counter work as before. Render resolution, texture filtering
and shadow resolution apply to it. It needs Vulkan 1.3 (dynamic rendering, push descriptors);
without them the game falls back to xemu's drawing.

`NGB_RENDERER=xemu` draws with xemu's NV2A renderer instead, as before (on Steam:
`NGB_RENDERER=xemu %command%`). `NGB_RENDERER=mirror` keeps xemu drawing and showing the game
and renders with the new one unseen, for comparing (`NGB_D3D_DUMP=dir` writes its frames).

## Bring-up tools

- `kill -USR1 <pid>` prints the guest thread's host backtrace (every lifted function
  is a named `sub_XXXXXXXX`) and its guest registers. It needs no ptrace, so use it
  instead of gdb: gdb swallows the TF single-steps that the register traps depend on.
- `RECOMP_WATCHDOG_SECS=N` dumps guest state and exits after N seconds.
- `tools/feedback.sh [secs]` runs an instrumented build, records every
  indirect-branch target it reaches, reseeds function detection and regenerates.
  Run it after the game reaches new code.
- `XBOX_LOG_LEVEL=4` and `RECOMP_KERNEL_LOG_BUDGET=100000` give a full kernel and
  file trace.

The defaults in `bringup_defaults()` (`src/main.c`) stand in for hardware that isn't
modelled yet. Each one should disappear when the real thing exists.

```

`docs/renderer.md`:

```md
# A Direct3D-level renderer (replacing xemu's NV2A emulation)

Goal: draw Ninja Gaiden Black by implementing the Xbox Direct3D 8 API (XDK 5849, the
link-time-optimised D3D8LTCG build) on Vulkan, as SCDA-XBERecomp does for Splinter Cell:
Double Agent on Direct3D 12 (github.com/TGP482/SCDA-XBERecomp). The game's Direct3D calls never become NV2A push buffers; nothing emulates the
GPU. It is the default; `NGB_RENDERER=xemu` selects xemu's renderer.

## What NGB looks like (measured)

- Direct3D lives in the XBE's `D3D` section (0x3C5260-0x3D95E0) plus a few functions LTCG
  moved into `.text` (InsertFence 0x1A0AB2). XbSymbolDatabase names 97 of them, with their
  LTCG register conventions in the name (`_4__LTCG_eax1_ebx2`: 4 bytes of stack, argument 1
  in eax, 2 in ebx).
- Game code calls them (329 calls to SetRenderState_Simple, 51 to SetPixelShader, ...).
  141 game functions outside the library touch Direct3D's globals, inlined by LTCG, but only
  to update state in memory (SetTransform's matrix copy into the device at +0xDE0 and a dirty
  bit at 0x3D83D0); no game code writes the push buffer. So the renderer can read inlined
  state from the device at draw time and hook only the functions that emit GPU work.
- Push buffer pointer and limit: 0x3D5F20 / 0x3D5F24 (the static CDevice).

## Reused from SCDA

- `gpu/shaders.cpp`: vertex programs, fixed function and the pixel combiners to HLSL. Its
  output compiles to SPIR-V with glslang's HLSL front end unmodified (tested).
- `gpu/vertex.cpp`, `gpu/texture.cpp`: vertex formats, swizzling, texture decoding.
- `xdk/d3d8.cpp`: which API entry points to implement and how (the state model).
- New: a Vulkan backend in place of `gpu/d3d12.cpp` (window and swapchain from present_sdl).

## Milestones

1. Hooks: every Direct3D entry point moved out of the generated code behind a wrapper that
   calls the recompiled body unless the new renderer is on. NGB_D3D_TRACE logs the calls with
   their decoded arguments, to check the conventions against what the game passes.
2. Backend skeleton: Vulkan device on the game window, Clear and Swap. First picture: the
   clear colours of the boot screens.
3. Draws: streams, vertex shaders and fixed function, textures, render targets. Goal: the
   title screen and menus.
4. Pixel shaders, fog, alpha test, blending, stencil, shadows, CopyRects, render to texture.
   Goal: chapter 1 gameplay.
5. Parity: every scene, the quality settings (render scale, filtering, shadow resolution),
   the recomp's menus, then the switch of default.

## Status (2026-10-12)

- `NGB_RENDERER=d3d`: the renderer draws to the window. It shares xemu's Vulkan device
  (`xboxrecomp/src/nv2a_vk/host/nv2a_vk_share.h`: the device, a lock around queue submissions,
  and `nv2a_present_set_external`, a picture the presenter shows in place of its own). xemu's
  renderer keeps executing the push buffer for the fences and flips but its draws, clears,
  blits and surface traffic are off (`nv2a_vk_set_draws_off`; `NGB_D3D_KEEP_NV2A=1` keeps
  them, unseen). Each Swap copies the front buffer to one of three images handed to the
  presenter, so the title's next frame never races the blit.
- The swap turns the back buffer's surface object to the other buffer's memory, so the render
  target is read again from that object after each Swap. The frame's first clear comes before
  any SetRenderTarget: with the address from before the swap it cleared the picture just shown,
  which a camera cut's cross-fade then copied (the whole screen the fog colour for a frame) and
  the menus' feedback backdrop (each frame the last one with the backdrop at 24% over it) drew
  over black.
- The hooks run as runtime host sections (`compat_host_enter/leave`): a guest thread parked
  by the scheduler while holding the queue lock stalled the PFIFO thread for good.
- Quality settings come from the presenter (`nv2a_quality_get`): display-sized targets render
  at the render scale, small depth-only targets (the shadow map) at the shadow scale, other
  small targets (the scarf simulation) 1:1; smooth filtering is linear/anisotropic/trilinear.
- Pixel shaders are read from the handle at SetPixelShader (the object holds the definition at
  +0xC): most were created before the hooks saw a CreatePixelShader, and without them the
  shadow pass drew with the fixed function stages and blackened the scene.
- Shadow comparison: the console tests texel OP reference, Vulkan reference OP texel; the
  function is swapped (`swap[8] = {0, 4, 2, 6, 1, 5, 3, 7}`).
- CPU: about 4 cores busy in gameplay against 3.3 for xemu alone (mirror mode, both drawing:
  8.7). Draws are recorded and submitted on the title's thread, one submission a frame.

Next: more scenes and chapters, Windows (the Proton build), Steam Deck performance, the
debug knobs out once it is the default.

- Default since 2026-10-12 (`NGB_RENDERER` unset means `d3d`; `xemu` for the old renderer).
- Fixed-function vertex blending (D3DRS_VERTEXBLEND, the NV2A skin modes 1-6): the characters
  are skinned with it, position and normal over world matrices 0-3 weighted by v1 (modes 1, 3,
  5 give one weight fewer than matrices, the last 1 - the others). Without it every vertex took
  world 0 and the joints (knees, shoulders, hips) came apart into holes.
- Pixel centres: the console's are at whole coordinates, Vulkan's at halves. Everything is drawn half a
  console pixel right and down (the vertex epilogue for programs and screen-space vertices, the viewport
  matrix for fixed function), as xemu has it: menu pieces meeting at x.5 no longer leave a hairline gap
  (a red line through the pause menu's blade at 8x), and frames line up with xemu's to the pixel. The
  SCDA full screen quad stretch (and its texture coordinate correction) is gone with it.
- At render scale 8 in chapter 1: GPU busy about 24% against xemu's 51%; CPU about 4.2 cores against
  3.4 (the hooks, the per-draw state copy and hashing every bound texture's bytes each draw are the
  likely costs to cut next).
- A setting change (render scale, MSAA) keeps each display-sized target's picture: the old image is
  blitted into the new one, and an MSAA image is refilled from it by a full screen draw before the next
  pass (FillMs; also after a copy into an MSAA target). The pause menu's still of the game no longer goes
  black until the game draws it again. `NGB_D3D_QUALITY_FLIP=n` alternates MSAA and scale every n s
  (testing).
- V8U8 bump maps (format 0x28/0x17, G8B8's codes) are read through an R8G8B8A8_SNORM view when the next
  stage bump-maps from them (texture mode 6 or 7), so the filter blends signed values -- read unsigned,
  texels either side of zero blended through the wrong range: the chapter 2 water's contour lines.
- Anisotropic filtering on: single-level opaque textures get a generated mip chain (2:1 linear blits),
  DXT1/2/3 ones decoded to BGRA for it (DecodeBC) -- most of the game's world textures have no mipmaps
  and sparkle in the distance otherwise (xemu's smooth mode did this for BGRA only). `NGB_D3D_MIPLOG=1`
  lists single-level textures; `dump_dir/burst.now` dumps the next 40 frames.
- The shader cache (backend.cpp, ShaderCache): recipes.bin (each module's inputs, pipeline keys),
  spirv.bin (SPIR-V by the hash of its HLSL), pipelines.bin (VkPipelineCache) under
  $NV2A_SHADER_CACHE/d3d; a prewarm thread makes them all at startup, plus the shipped seed
  (share/NinjaGaidenBlack/d3d-seed.bin; NGB_D3D_SEED_RECORD=<file> records one, vertex programs as
  default.xbe offsets). First chapter-1 combat went from 24 compile hitches (300 ms in all, up to 83 ms
  in one frame) to none. NGB_D3D_HITCHLOG=1 logs frames held up by compiling. xemu's own pipeline
  prewarm is off while it draws nothing (NV2A_NO_PREWARM).
- Two frames in flight (EndFrame): the game records frame N+1 while the GPU draws N; Submit() is the
  full sync for callers that destroy or read back; replaced textures are retired to a graveyard until
  no frame in flight can use them; the presenter waits on the frame with a barrier (same queue). At 10x
  with 8x MSAA (GPU bound): 31 -> 36 fps; 10x with 4x MSAA holds 60.

- Shaders and pipelines a draw needs that nothing has made yet (not in the cache, the seed or the startup
  warm-up) are made on a thread of their own and the draw is left out until they are, a frame or two,
  instead of the frame waiting for them (a hitch: 10-80 ms each on a first sight). `NGB_D3D_SYNC_COMPILE=1`
  makes them at once as before. The pipelines warmed at startup are also made for the anti-aliasing in use
  (and again when it changes): each holds one sample count, and the seed's were recorded without MSAA.

- The gamma ramp (D3DDevice_SetGammaRamp: the game's Screen Adjustment -- gamma, brightness, contrast) is
  applied as the front buffer is copied for the presenter, through a 256-entry table per channel; at the
  game's default (an identity ramp) the plain copy as before. `NGB_D3D_GAMMALOG=1` logs each ramp.

- A fixed-function stage reading a texture with none bound is off (its output the stage before's), as the
  console's D3D sets up its combiners: the game's fades are drawn TEXTURE x TFACTOR without a texture and
  show their vertex colour. Read as white, Game Over's fade painted its sepia texture factor over the
  screen each frame and the motion blur fed it back to a flat pale yellow.

```

`packaging/appimage/Dockerfile`:

```
# Build environment for the Ninja Gaiden Black AppImage (packaging/appimage/build.sh):
# Ubuntu 22.04, so the program needs no glibc newer than 2.35 and runs on
# SteamOS, Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12, Fedora 36+ and other current systems.
# The first RUN matches the Wind Waker AppImage's environment layer for layer,
# so the two share Docker's cache.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

ARG LLVM_VERSION=22
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates wget gnupg lsb-release software-properties-common git file \
        python3 python3-pip pkg-config \
    && add-apt-repository -y ppa:ubuntu-toolchain-r/test \
    && apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        g++-13 libstdc++-13-dev \
        libx11-dev libxext-dev libxrandr-dev libxcursor-dev libxfixes-dev libxi-dev libxss-dev libxtst-dev \
        libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev wayland-protocols libdecor-0-dev libegl1-mesa-dev libgl-dev \
        libgbm-dev libdrm-dev libvulkan-dev libpulse-dev libpipewire-0.3-dev libasound2-dev libdbus-1-dev \
        libudev-dev \
    && wget -qO /tmp/llvm.sh https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh \
    && bash /tmp/llvm.sh ${LLVM_VERSION} \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends clang-${LLVM_VERSION} lld-${LLVM_VERSION} llvm-${LLVM_VERSION} \
    && for tool in clang clang++ ld.lld llvm-strip llvm-profdata; do \
           ln -sf /usr/bin/${tool}-${LLVM_VERSION} /usr/local/bin/${tool}; done \
    && python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir "cmake>=3.25,<4" ninja patchelf \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* /tmp/llvm.sh

# The runtime's own: glib (the xemu GPU model's QEMU shim), libepoxy (the
# toolkit's OpenGL D3D backend, linked though unused here).
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        libglib2.0-dev libepoxy-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# SDL2, newer than 22.04's 2.0.20 (Steam Deck and current pads, PipeWire),
# with every video/audio backend loaded at run time from the player's system.
ARG SDL2_VERSION=2.32.10
RUN wget -qO /tmp/sdl.tar.gz https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases/download/release-${SDL2_VERSION}/SDL2-${SDL2_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf /tmp/sdl.tar.gz -C /tmp \
    && cmake -S /tmp/SDL2-${SDL2_VERSION} -B /tmp/sdl-build -G Ninja \
         -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
         -DSDL_STATIC=OFF -DSDL_SHARED=ON -DSDL_TEST=OFF \
    && cmake --build /tmp/sdl-build && cmake --install /tmp/sdl-build \
    && rm -rf /tmp/sdl.tar.gz /tmp/SDL2-${SDL2_VERSION} /tmp/sdl-build

# glslang with its C interface, static, without the optimizer (and so
# without SPIRV-Tools): the renderer compiles its shaders at run time.
ARG GLSLANG_VERSION=16.6.0
RUN git clone --depth 1 -b ${GLSLANG_VERSION} https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glslang /tmp/glslang \
    && cmake -S /tmp/glslang -B /tmp/glslang-build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
         -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
         -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DENABLE_OPT=OFF -DGLSLANG_TESTS=OFF -DENABLE_GLSLANG_BINARIES=OFF \
         -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON \
    && cmake --build /tmp/glslang-build && cmake --install /tmp/glslang-build \
    && rm -rf /tmp/glslang /tmp/glslang-build

# Qt 6 Widgets for the first-run setup window (ngb-setup), bundled with its
# xcb and Wayland platform plugins.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        qt6-base-dev qt6-qpa-plugins qt6-wayland libgl1-mesa-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

`packaging/appimage/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Ninja Gaiden Black (static recompilation) for Linux as an AppImage.
#
#   packaging/appimage/build.sh [out-dir]      (default build/appimage)
#
# Compiles the game and the xboxrecomp toolkit (xboxrecomp/ in this
# repository, or XBOXRECOMP_DIR) in an Ubuntu 22.04 container (Dockerfile here), so the
# AppImage needs only glibc 2.35, and packs it with appimagetool into
# <out-dir>/NinjaGaidenBlack-x86_64.AppImage.
#
# The recompiled code must already be generated (tools/pipeline.sh). The
# AppImage holds the program and the libraries a system may lack (SDL2,
# glib, libepoxy; libstdc++ linked in). It holds no game data:
# the first launch asks for the player's disc image and installs the files
# into ~/.local/share/NinjaGaidenBlack/game (see src/install.c).
set -euo pipefail

here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
repo=$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)
toolkit=$(cd "${XBOXRECOMP_DIR:-$repo/xboxrecomp}" && pwd)
out=$(mkdir -p "${1:-$repo/build/appimage}" && cd "${1:-$repo/build/appimage}" && pwd)
image=ngb-build:jammy
jobs=${JOBS:-$(nproc)}

[ -n "$(ls "$repo"/src/recomp/gen/*.c 2>/dev/null)" ] ||
    { echo "No generated code: run tools/pipeline.sh first." >&2; exit 1; }

docker build -q -t "$image" "$here" >/dev/null

# The toolkit is the copy in the repository (xboxrecomp/), or XBOXRECOMP_DIR
# mounted beside it.
mounts=(-v "$repo":/work/ngb-recomp -v "$out":/out)
toolkit_in=/work/ngb-recomp/xboxrecomp
if [ "$toolkit" != "$repo/xboxrecomp" ]; then
    mounts+=(-v "$toolkit":/work/xboxrecomp:ro)
    toolkit_in=/work/xboxrecomp
fi

docker run --rm -m 14g -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e HOME=/tmp "${mounts[@]}" \
    "$image" bash -euc '
cmake -S /work/ngb-recomp -B /out/build -G Ninja \
    -DXBOXRECOMP_DIR='"$toolkit_in"' \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
    -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc -fuse-ld=lld" \
    -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/usr/local >/out/configure.log
ninja -C /out/build -j'"$jobs"' >/out/build.log

app=/out/AppDir
rm -rf "$app"
mkdir -p "$app/usr/bin" "$app/usr/lib"
cp /out/build/NinjaGaidenBlack /out/build/ngb-setup "$app/usr/bin/"
llvm-strip "$app/usr/bin/NinjaGaidenBlack" "$app/usr/bin/ngb-setup"

# Bundle what a system may lack; never glibc, the Vulkan loader or GPU and
# window-system libraries, which must be the systems own.
for lib in $(ldd "$app/usr/bin/NinjaGaidenBlack" | awk "/=>/ {print \$3}"); do
    case "$(basename "$lib")" in
    libSDL2-2.0.so*|libglib-2.0.so*|libpcre.so*|libepoxy.so*) cp -L "$lib" "$app/usr/lib/" ;;
    esac
done

# The setup window: Qt and what it needs that a system may lack, and the
# xcb and Wayland platform plugins (found through qt.conf beside it).
qtp=$(dirname "$(dirname "$(find /usr/lib -path "*qt6/plugins/platforms/libqxcb.so" | head -1)")")
mkdir -p "$app/usr/plugins"
for d in platforms/libqxcb.so platforms/libqwayland-generic.so \
         wayland-shell-integration wayland-decoration-client platforminputcontexts; do
    mkdir -p "$app/usr/plugins/$(dirname "$d")"
    cp -rL "$qtp/$d" "$app/usr/plugins/$(dirname "$d")/"
done
printf "[Paths]\nPrefix = ..\nPlugins = plugins\n" > "$app/usr/bin/qt.conf"
# Never bundled: glibc, the C++ runtime, GPU, X11/Wayland, font and
# session libraries, which must be the systems own.
system_lib="^(ld-linux|libc|libm|libdl|librt|libpthread|libresolv|libutil|libstdc\+\+|libgcc_s|libGL|libEGL|libGLX|libGLdispatch|libOpenGL|libdrm|libgbm|libvulkan|libX11|libXau|libXdmcp|libXext|libXrender|libxcb\.so|libxcb-(shm|render|xfixes|randr|shape|sync|xkb|xinput|glx|dri2|dri3|present)\.so|libwayland-|libfontconfig|libfreetype|libharfbuzz|libexpat|libz\.|libdbus-1|libudev|libsystemd|libgpg-error|libselinux|libmount|libblkid|libffi|liblzma|liblz4|libzstd|libgcrypt|libcap|libbsd|libmd\.)"
bundle_deps() {
    ldd "$1" | awk "/=>/ {print \$3}" | while read -r lib; do
        b=$(basename "$lib")
        echo "$b" | grep -Eq "$system_lib" && continue
        [ -e "$app/usr/lib/$b" ] || cp -L "$lib" "$app/usr/lib/"
    done
}
bundle_deps "$app/usr/bin/ngb-setup"
for so in $(find "$app/usr/plugins" -name "*.so"); do bundle_deps "$so"; done

patchelf --set-rpath "\$ORIGIN/../lib" "$app/usr/bin/NinjaGaidenBlack" "$app/usr/bin/ngb-setup"
for so in "$app"/usr/lib/*.so*; do patchelf --set-rpath "\$ORIGIN" "$so"; done
for so in $(find "$app/usr/plugins" -name "*.so"); do patchelf --set-rpath "\$ORIGIN/../../lib" "$so"; done
echo "Bundled:"; ls "$app/usr/lib"
echo "Needs from the system:"; readelf -d "$app/usr/bin/NinjaGaidenBlack" | sed -n "s/.*NEEDED.*\[\(.*\)\]/  \1/p"
'

app=$out/AppDir
# Pipelines recorded while testing, built in the background at startup so a
# first run does not stall on them (see NV2A_SHADER_SEED in src/main.c). The
# game's vertex programs are not in it: the renderer reads them from the
# player's default.xbe (tools/strip_shader_seed.py).
# The Direct3D renderer's seed (src/d3d/vk/backend.cpp, the shader cache): its shaders and pipelines
# are made in the background at the first start; vertex programs are places in the player's XBE.
mkdir -p "$app/usr/share/NinjaGaidenBlack"
cp "$here/../d3d-seed.bin" "$app/usr/share/NinjaGaidenBlack/d3d-seed.bin"
mkdir -p "$app/usr/share/NinjaGaidenBlack/shader-seed"
cp "$here/../shader-seed/states.bin" "$here/../shader-seed/pipelines.bin" \
   "$app/usr/share/NinjaGaidenBlack/shader-seed/"
# The fonts built into the program (SIL Open Font License): their licences.
mkdir -p "$app/usr/share/licenses/NinjaGaidenBlack"
cp "$repo"/assets/fonts/OFL-*.txt "$app/usr/share/licenses/NinjaGaidenBlack/"
cp "$repo"/assets/prompts/License-Xelu.txt "$app/usr/share/licenses/NinjaGaidenBlack/"
cp "$repo/LICENSE" "$repo/THIRD_PARTY.md" "$app/usr/share/licenses/NinjaGaidenBlack/"
cp "$repo/src/d3d/NOTICE" "$app/usr/share/licenses/NinjaGaidenBlack/NOTICE-renderer.txt"
cp "$toolkit/LICENSE" "$app/usr/share/licenses/NinjaGaidenBlack/LICENSE-xboxrecomp.txt"
cp "$toolkit/NOTICE" "$app/usr/share/licenses/NinjaGaidenBlack/NOTICE-xboxrecomp.txt"
cp "$toolkit/LICENSES/LGPL-2.1.txt" "$app/usr/share/licenses/NinjaGaidenBlack/"
cp "$here/ngb.png" "$app/ninja-gaiden-black.png"
cp "$here/ngb.png" "$app/.DirIcon"
cat > "$app/ninja-gaiden-black.desktop" <<'DESKTOP'
[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=Ninja Gaiden Black
GenericName=Ninja Gaiden Black (static recompilation)
Comment=Ninja Gaiden Black, recompiled for Linux with Vulkan; asks for your own disc image
Exec=NinjaGaidenBlack %f
Icon=ninja-gaiden-black
Categories=Game;ActionGame;
Terminal=false
DESKTOP
cat > "$app/AppRun" <<'APPRUN'
#!/bin/sh
# The program finds its bundled libraries through its rpath, so the tools it
# starts (the file dialog, bsdtar) keep the system's.
here="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
exec "$here/usr/bin/NinjaGaidenBlack" "$@"
APPRUN
chmod +x "$app/AppRun"

tool=$here/.cache/appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage
if [ ! -x "$tool" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$here/.cache"
    wget -qO "$tool" https://github.com/AppImage/appimagetool/releases/download/continuous/appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage
    chmod +x "$tool"
fi
ARCH=x86_64 "$tool" --appimage-extract-and-run --no-appstream "$app" \
    "$out/NinjaGaidenBlack-x86_64.AppImage" >"$out/appimagetool.log" 2>&1 ||
    { tail -20 "$out/appimagetool.log"; exit 1; }
ls -la "$out/NinjaGaidenBlack-x86_64.AppImage"

`packaging/macos/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Native Apple Silicon app, with the first-run installer and no game data.
# Generate src/recomp/gen with tools/pipeline.sh before building.
set -euo pipefail
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
repo=$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)
out=$(mkdir -p "${1:-$repo/build/macos-release}" && cd "${1:-$repo/build/macos-release}" && pwd)
prefix=${NGB_MAC_PREFIX:-$(brew --prefix)}
cmake -S "$repo" -B "$out/build" -G Ninja \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
    -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$prefix" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DXBOXRECOMP_DIR="${XBOXRECOMP_DIR:-$repo/xboxrecomp}" >"$out/configure.log"
cmake --build "$out/build" -j"${JOBS:-$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)}" >"$out/build.log"
app="$out/Ninja Gaiden Black.app"
rm -rf "$app"
python3 "$here/bundle.py" "$out/build" "$app" --prefix "$prefix" \
    --toolkit "${XBOXRECOMP_DIR:-$repo/xboxrecomp}"
rm -f "$out/NinjaGaidenBlack-macos-arm64.zip"
ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent "$app" "$out/NinjaGaidenBlack-macos-arm64.zip"
echo "Packed: $out/NinjaGaidenBlack-macos-arm64.zip"
